CZ_NAME: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR 30 TO 60NM
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Gale force winds behind a strong cold front swept across the entire coastal waters off San Diego County. At the peak, winds were sustained 43 mph with gusts to 52 mph at San Clemente Island. Elswhere, the San Clemente Basin Buoy measured a sustained wind of 40 mph with gusts to 47 mph. Similar wind speeds were observed along the coast as well, including several wind gusts in excess of 50 mph. The gale generated large, short period waves that resulted in very hazardous boating conditions. The most extreme example of this was at Newport Beach where 10-12 foot waves were observed with a 3 second period. Further south, the Oceanside Harbor entrance buoy reported a 16 foot wave with a 9 second period. No reports of significant damage have been received at this time, which may indicate that mariners heeded the warning and remained in harbor.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: NA

CZ_NAME: CP HENLOPEN TO FENWICK IS DE OUT 20NM
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Three men (20-year-old, 21-year-old and 25-year-old) were rescued from the frigid waters off of Cape Henlopen on the afternoon of the 16th after their kayaks overturned. All were treated for hypothermia and released. The men left the Capes Shore Beach between the state fishing pier and the Cape Shores pier at about 315 p.m. EDT on the 16th and were headed for Lewes. They were about 600 yards offshore, where the winds and waves increased. Winds were estimated at about 25 knots. A large wave hit the two-man kayak. It took on water and a panicked man leaned into the waves and overturned the kayak. They were unable to right it. They then took turns in and out of the remaining one-man kayak which after about 15 minutes also was flipped. They were spotted in the water by a Cape Henlopen State Park ranger. A Delaware State Police helicopter and a patrol boat of the State Division of Fish and Wildlife Enforcement assisted in the rescue. They were in the water for about 40 minutes and ocean water temperatures were in the mid 50s.

CZ_NAME: WIND PT LT WI TO WINTHROP HBR IL
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Rapidly developing low pressure moved across western Ohio and southeast Lower Michigan during the overnight period of October 19th and morning of October 20th.  An associated strong pressure gradient and lingering unstable conditions over Lake Michigan allowed strong gusty north to northeast winds to mix down to the lake surface.  The lake surface temperature at this time was estimated to be in the 54 to 58 degree range.  Wind gusts reached 50 to 70 mph along the lake shore.  The strong winds caused high waves of 12 to 16 feet.  The strong winds and high waves caused extensive damage to boats in the South Shore Yacht Club, mainly due to an eroding and failing breakwall protecting the southern part of Milwaukee Harbor.  Three boats were totally destroyed at the yacht club.  Four others were washed ashore and were able to be salvaged.  Two of the destroyed boats were sunk.  One person at the Club, while trying to secure a boat with a rope line, was tossed about on the boat due to wave action and injured (directly-related).
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Measured at 21st Century Prep School.

The cyclone eventually became a Tropical Storm and slowly moved to the southwest and finally made landfall along the northeast Florida coast. The two victims were swept into Lake Michigan by high waves crashing onto the Sheboygan harbor north break wall.  The two were trying to recover fishing equipment which had fallen into the lake the day before.  A third person was also washed into the lake by the high waves, but survived due to holding onto a nearby ladder.  The first victim's body was located the next day, Saturday, August 11th.  The second victim was found the following day, on Sunday, August 12th.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Sustained winds of 32 knots gusting to 34-36 knots caused high waves on the Sheboygan harbor break wall.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A family of five (husband, wife, three children under the age of 10) set out on a kayak to tour the Apostle Islands at around 100 pm CDT. Wind and waves were nearly calm when the family set out from Madeline Island on a sit on top type of kayak. The winds picked up by 4 pm becoming east-southeast at 5-15 mph with waves building to 1-3 feet, causing the kayak to overturn, sending the family into the water.  All occupants were wearing life jackets, however, water temperatures were around 60 degrees and they were not wearing wet suits. The father and children tried to swim to the nearest island while the mother remained with the boat. She had a cell phone and tried to text for help, but cell coverage was poor. A text message from the mother went through around 8:30 pm to her sister, who then contacted police. Search teams were deployed and the wife was found alive just after 10 pm. The father and two of the children were found deceased after midnight on the 31st and the third child was found deceased at about 10 am the same day. The cause of death of the father and children was hypothermia due to the 60 degree water.

EVENT_NARRATIVE: A prolonged period of northeast winds led to 2 to 4 foot waves at the head of Lake Superior. Winds were on the downward trend the morning of the 30th with gusts to around 22mph in thundershowers that moved through earlier in the morning, with rain ending around 10AM. Three boaters in aboard a 21 foot Monark Aluminum Hulled boat departed from Superior Bay and entered Lake Superior through the Superior Entry when they turned northwest to parallel Minnesota Point. Waves caused the engine to be overcome with water, and subsequent large waves turned the boat, later flipping it upside down in the water. The boat capsized around 11AM, sending the the occupants into the water. All were wearing life jackets, but they were not zipped up. Two of the boaters reached the shore safely, but the third occupant did not and his body was recovered by the Duluth Fire Department. A Small Craft Advisory was in effect at the time along with a Beach Hazards Statement citing a high risk for rip currents in the area.

Westerly flow pinned the Atlantic coast sea breeze to the coast and gave an early start to the Gulf coast sea breeze shifting inland across northeast Florida. These storms produced gusts between 45 to 55 mph at Marineland, St. Augustine and Mayport. Also, lightning struck a house in Neptune beach causing a house fire. Street flooding and heavy rain in Jacksonville Beach and Clay county were caused by training storms moving northeastward along a line that set up extending from Jacksonville Beach to Ocala.

CZ_NAME: VERMILION TO AVON POINT OH
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A deepening and occluded surface low moved north-northeastward from eastern Iowa to northern Wisconsin during the late morning through early evening of the 5th. This low interacted with a strong surface high pressure ridge to its east, which lead to a tight mean sea-level pressure gradient across Lake Erie and vicinity, including northern Ohio. The tight pressure gradient and diurnal convective mixing of the boundary layer over land, tapping into stronger flow aloft, resulted in southerly to south-southwesterly surface wind gusts as strong as 30 to 40 knots in northern Ohio and over adjacent waters of Lake Erie. Unfortunately a kayaker ventured onto Lake Erie and perished while encountering the gusty winds and sizable waves. A Small Craft Advisory was in effect.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: FOX 8 Cleveland reported a 30-year old male kayaker went missing just offshore Miller Road Park in Avon Lake around 2 PM EDT. Location is estimated. He was wearing a life jacket. The Huron Light C-MAN Station (HHLO1) was the nearest weather station reporting observations at the time of the incident. The reported gust at 2 PM EDT was used as an estimate. On December 10th, 2022, the man's kayak was found along the Lake Erie shore in Fort Erie, Ontario.

Behind the front, westerly surface winds around 10 to 15 knots and waves no larger than one to three feet affected Lake Erie during the morning of the 6th. EVENT_NARRATIVE: A trade-wind surge affecting eastern Micronesia with winds estimated to be around 20 to 25 knots, according to satellite scatterometer data. Wind waves with a mixed trade swell and longer period north swell, generated choppy seas, estimated to be around 8 to 11 feet based on satellite altimetry, around Majuro Atoll near the end of December. On December 30th a motorboat left Majuro between 1700LST to 1730LST (1500ChST to 1530ChST) in the late afternoon and was heading east to Arno Atoll, roughly 30 miles away. The boat had seven individuals onboard (5 men and 2 women) and was reported missing at 2100LST (1900ChST) when the boat did not arrive at Arno as scheduled. Rescuers found 2 survivors, 3 men, while only 1 male body was recovered about half way between Majuro and Arno Atolls as the boat had sunk. The other 2 men and 2 women were not found and presumed lost. Age of the victims was not given and not estimate on the cost of the boat was available.
